chunks: Which elements are used as dopants. The question: What elements are typically used for doping?
Dopants are the elements added to silicon to make it N-type or P-type. Silicon has four outer electrons.
An element with five outer electrons gives an extra electron, which makes N-type. An element with three leaves a missing electron, which makes P-type.
You can find the right elements by looking at the periodic table.
Picture a square dance in which every dancer needs exactly four partners' hands. If a newcomer with five hands joins, one hand is left free.
If a newcomer with only three hands joins, one hand is missing. The free hand is an extra electron, and the missing one is a hole.
The analogy breaks down since atoms bond with electrons, not hands, but the counting works.
Dopants for a Group IV host sit one column on either side. Left column (one electron short) makes holes, right column (one extra electron) makes free electrons.
Elements in the same column as the host are isoelectronic and do not dope.
Valence electrons: the outer electrons that form bonds. Silicon has four. Donor: a dopant with five valence electrons that gives an extra electron, N-type.
Acceptor: a dopant with three valence electrons that makes a hole, P-type. Group III, IV and V: columns of the periodic table, with three, four and five valence electrons.
Phosphorus is in Group V, with five valence electrons. Replace one silicon atom with it, and four electrons bond to neighbors while the fifth is free. That is a donor.
Boron is in Group III, with three, so one bond lacks an electron. That is an acceptor. Arsenic is another donor and boron is the usual acceptor. That is the whole idea.
"In silicon, donors are Group V atoms, with an extra valence electron: phosphorus, arsenic and antimony give N-type.
Acceptors are Group III atoms with one fewer: boron mainly, and gallium, aluminium or indium in special cases, give P-type.
Arsenic diffuses slowly so it's used for shallow source and drain; phosphorus diffuses faster and goes in wells; boron is the standard P-type dopant.
In compound semiconductors the dopants differ, such as silicon and magnesium in GaN."
